title: Terms of a Massachusetts sale of hypodermic syringes and needles: s. 27 as amended in 2018, the s. 32I(d) carve-out and the s. 25K point-of-sale insert
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 27 provides that hypodermic syringes or hypodermic needles for the administration of controlled substances by injection may be sold in the commonwealth only by a pharmacist or wholesale druggist licensed under the provisions of chapter 112, a manufacturer of or dealer in surgical supplies or a manufacturer of or dealer in embalming supplies. The section states no prescription, age, identification, quantity or record requirement. Sections 47 and 48 of chapter 208 of the Acts of 2018 struck from s. 27 the words ', but only to persons who have attained the age of 18 years and' and struck its second sentence, which as enacted by chapter 172 of the Acts of 2006 had provided that when selling hypodermic syringes or hypodermic needles without a prescription, a pharmacist or wholesale druggist must require proof of identification that validates the individual's age; section 49 of the same act struck from s. 32I the words 'to persons over the age of 18'. Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 32I(a) no person shall sell, possess or purchase with intent to sell, or manufacture with intent to sell drug paraphernalia knowing, or under circumstances where one reasonably should know, that it will be used for purposes that include introducing a controlled substance into the human body in violation of chapter 94C, and under s. 32I(d) the section shall not apply to the sale of hypodermic syringes or hypodermic needles pursuant to s. 27. Under M.G.L. c. 111, s. 25K the department shall develop an educational insert to accompany the sale of hypodermic syringes and needles, including but not limited to information on the proper use of hypodermic syringes and needles, the risk of blood-borne diseases that may result from their use and methods for preventing contracting or transmitting such diseases, proper hypodermic syringe and needle disposal practices, and the toll-free telephone numbers of the commonwealth's AIDS and Hepatitis C hotlines and the Massachusetts Substance Abuse Information and Education Helpline, and the educational insert shall be provided to purchasers of hypodermic syringes or needles at the point of sale.
exam_relevance: Tests who may sell hypodermic syringes and needles, that the current s. 27 carries no age or identification condition after the 2018 amendments, that a s. 27 sale is outside the paraphernalia offense, and that the Department's educational insert is to be provided to purchasers at the point of sale.

exceptions: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 32I does not apply to the sale of hypodermic syringes or hypodermic needles pursuant to s. 27.
common_confusions: Applying the age-18 limit or the proof-of-age identification requirement that chapter 208 of the Acts of 2018 struck from s. 27.
Section 25K provides that the insert shall be provided to purchasers at the point of sale but does not name who provides it.
Section 27 names categories of seller; it does not address the seller's employees.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, ss. 27 and 32I and M.G.L. c. 111, s. 25K read on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-16, together with chapter 172 of the Acts of 2006 and sections 47 through 49 of chapter 208 of the Acts of 2018.
